category_info.mature_height: 3-6 m in the ground; 1.5-2.5 m in large containers
category_info.hardiness: frost sensitive; best in USDA zones 9-11 or as a container plant moved indoors in winter
category_info.pruning_season: light pruning after harvest; remove suckers below the graft at any time
category_info.watering_need: deep watering when the top 5 cm of soil is dry; citrus dislike both drought and soggy roots
common_issues: Root rot in poorly drained soil

observations.symptom: Interveinal chlorosis: yellow leaves with distinctly green veins
observations.location: Newest leaves at the branch tips
observations.evidence: Young leaves show bright yellow blades while the vein network remains dark green

observations.symptom: Curved silvery trails inside some leaves
observations.evidence: Winding pale tunnels under the leaf surface are visible on close inspection

possible_causes.name: Iron or zinc deficiency (likely high soil pH)
possible_causes.reason: Yellow young leaves with green veins on citrus are textbook micronutrient deficiency, usually caused by alkaline soil or overwatering blocking iron uptake

possible_causes.name: Citrus leaf miner damage
possible_causes.reason: Silvery serpentine mines in leaves are caused by leaf miner larvae; it is cosmetic but stresses young growth

possible_causes.name: Overwatering contributing to nutrient lockout
possible_causes.reason: Chronically wet soil prevents roots from absorbing iron even when it is present

recommended_actions.action: Check watering and drainage: let the top 5 cm of soil dry before deep watering
recommended_actions.reason: Restoring air in the root zone often fixes nutrient uptake without any fertilizer change

recommended_actions.action: Feed with a citrus-specific fertilizer containing micronutrients (chelated iron, zinc, manganese)
recommended_actions.reason: Citrus blends match the pH and micronutrient profile citrus needs

recommended_actions.action: Leave leaf-miner mines alone on mature trees; prune only heavily mined young shoots
recommended_actions.reason: The damage is mostly cosmetic and natural predators keep it in check

seasonal_context: Citrus flush new growth in spring and autumn; deficiencies show up exactly when young leaves demand the most iron.
what_to_monitor: Whether the newest flush comes out green after feeding and drying adjustments
Yellowing spreading to older leaves, which would suggest a different cause
limitations: Soil pH cannot be measured from a photo; a soil test confirms the diagnosis
Nutrient deficiencies of iron, zinc and manganese look similar at this scale
follow_up_questions: Is the plant in the ground or a container, and what water do you use (tap, well, rain)?
When was it last fertilized, and with what product?
